Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $p:T_K\to K$ be the projection of the chosen normal-disk tube. Orient each normal disk so that its positive tangent direction followed by its oriented normal basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$. A **meridian** $\mu$ is the oriented boundary of one such normal disk. A **degree-one parallel curve** is a simple closed curve $\lambda$ in $T_K$ for which $p|_\lambda:\lambda\to K$ has degree $+1$. required_hypotheses: Let $X$ be a four-dimensional manifold with boundary and let $W$ be a compact surface with boundary. An embedding $e:(W,\partial W)\to(X,\partial X)$ is proper when $e^{-1}(\partial X)=\partial W$. It is locally flat at an interior point of $W$ when there are neighborhoods of the point and its image and a homeomorphism of pairs from those neighborhoods to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$, with the standard linear plane $\mathbb R^2\subset\mathbb R^4$. It is locally flat at a boundary point when there are such neighborhoods and a homeomorphism of pairs to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$, where $\mathbb R^4_+=\{x_4\geq0\}$ and $\mathbb R^2_+=\{x_2=x_3=0,\ x_4\geq0\}$; the line $\partial\mathbb R^2_+$ lies in $\partial\mathbb R^4_+$. A collar of a boundary circle of $W$ is an embedding of that circle times $[0,\varepsilon)$ into $W$ that is the identity on the circle at parameter $0$; a concordance collar is required to agree with the corresponding product collar of the ambient end. A smooth proper surface has the analogous smooth charts and collars, which are also topological locally flat charts.

required_hypotheses:
Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty oriented smooth link, with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L$ formed by deleting the interiors of pairwise-disjoint chosen closed normal-disk tubes, and basepoint $b\in E_L$. For a knot, $r=1$ and $E_L=E_K$. The full meridian abelianization group is $H_L=H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, with the positive normal-disk meridians as its ordered basis. Choose a finite-rank free abelian group $H$ of positive rank and an epimorphism $\chi:H_L\to H$; write $\psi=\chi\circ\mathrm{ab}:G\to H$ for the induced map from $G=\pi_1(E_L,b)$. The identity choice $H=H_L$ is the full multivariable deck map; a coloring may identify its variables only through the explicitly stated map $\chi$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, let $d\ge1$, and let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$, the commutative Laurent-polynomial ring with monomial basis $H$, and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$. On row vectors define the right $\mathbb F[G]$ action by $v\cdot g=v\rho(g)\psi(g)$, where $\psi(g)$ is central multiplication by its monomial in $\Lambda$.
